title: Where Is the Largest Card?
problem: Ten distinct cards are shuffled uniformly. What is the probability that the largest card appears among the first three positions?

hints.text: Every position is equally likely to contain the largest card.
Three of the ten symmetric positions are favorable.

solution.setup: Track only the position occupied by the unique largest card.
solution.reasoning: A uniform shuffle places that card in each of the ten positions with probability 1/10. The first three positions are favorable, so the probability is 3/10.
solution.sanityCheck: The first three positions make up 30% of all positions, and the distinguished card has no positional preference.

keyInsight: A distinguished object is uniform across symmetric positions even though the full permutation is complicated.
recognitionCues: One object is singled out after a uniform random permutation.
commonMistakes: Counting all 10! permutations when positional symmetry settles the question directly.
followUps: What is the probability the two largest cards are both in the first five positions?

verification.notes: Each of ten positions contains the maximum in 9! permutations.
